plan.request: Read email content, Create and manage drafts
plan.summary: Your requirements justify developer-owned credentials. Follow the scoped plan below and resolve conditional dependencies before launch.

next.title: Create a Google Cloud project and OAuth client
next.detail: Enable the Gmail API, configure the OAuth audience and branding, and create the appropriate web client. Keep client secrets out of frontend code.
next.doneWhen: The test app exists, its identity and callback configuration are recorded, and its credentials are stored server-side.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project and OAuth client
steps.detail: Enable the Gmail API, configure the OAuth audience and branding, and create the appropriate web client. Keep client secrets out of frontend code.
steps.doneWhen: The test app exists, its identity and callback configuration are recorded, and its credentials are stored server-side.

steps.title: Configure the permissions listed above
steps.detail: Add only the selected provider scopes in the appropriate consent or bot/user scope configuration. Reauthorize after scope changes.
steps.doneWhen: The configured grant matches the permission list and contains no unnecessary access.

steps.title: Copy the exact provider redirect URI from Composio
steps.detail: Begin a custom Auth Config for the correct toolkit and OAuth2 method. Copy its displayed redirect URI into the provider settings; this differs from your product’s Connect Link return URL.
steps.doneWhen: The exact redirect URI displayed by the Auth Config is saved in the provider app.

steps.title: Finish the custom Auth Config
steps.detail: Store provider credentials only in Composio/server-side secret configuration. Record the auth config ID; never paste credentials into this advisor.
steps.doneWhen: A usable auth config ID is recorded and its credentials are stored securely.

steps.title: Create a session scoped to the selected toolkit
steps.detail: Use a stable application user ID. Select your auth config when custom. Expose only required tools; session restrictions do not reduce the external provider’s grant.
steps.doneWhen: A session exists for the stable test user ID and the intended toolkit/auth config.

steps.title: Check the target organization’s installation policy
steps.detail: Test a representative account. If installation is restricted, ask its administrator to allow the app and requested access. No administrator turnaround is assumed.
steps.doneWhen: The described configuration is saved and ready for the next step.

steps.title: Authorize a representative account
steps.detail: Use the session’s Connect Link. Check completion and account identity in Composio; a successful callback alone is insufficient.
steps.doneWhen: The representative connected account reports successful authorization and the correct identity.

steps.title: Test: Read email content
steps.detail: Run this backend JavaScript with the authorized session created below. Replace the test inputs first. Use only a seeded test mailbox. For read-only access, inspect that no write scope was granted; do not test a write.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 with the selected test message id and payload. Record the actual response; this example has not been executed.
fields: TEST_MESSAGE_ID: list test messages with GET https://gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/me/messages?maxResults=1 and copy messages[0].id

steps.title: Test: Create and manage drafts
steps.detail: Run this backend JavaScript with the authorized session created below. Replace the test inputs first. Do not send the draft. gmail.compose also grants sending: enforce draft-only behavior in your tool layer.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 with draft id and message id; the message remains a draft. Record the actual response; this example has not been executed.
fields: Use the connected test account as From and a mailbox you control as To; generate raw with the supplied MIME line

steps.title: Check a testing or internal-use exception
steps.detail: Personal use, qualifying internal Workspace use and development/testing can qualify for verification exceptions. Check eligibility and test-user limits. Reassess before external production.
steps.doneWhen: The applicable approval or policy decision is recorded, with any outstanding owner and requirement.

steps.title: Review launch evidence and unresolved questions
steps.detail: Record actual results, customer-admin decisions and provider review outcomes. These personal checkmarks do not verify provider approval or execution success.
steps.doneWhen: Actual test results and outstanding launch gates are recorded.

timing.workBasis: Planning estimate, not a timed setup result. Assumes an existing provider account, a working app/backend and Composio access. Covers configuration and a first test connection; excludes building the feature, review preparation, security remediation and external waiting.
timing.wait: This plan checks a personal, internal or testing exception first. No verification wait is assigned until eligibility is confirmed. Reassess before expanding access.
timing.external: Customer administrator turnaround is not known. Check the target organization’s policy and actual permissions during the first connection test.

plan.integration: A custom configuration is recommended by your app ownership, permission or provider-model requirements. Managed OAuth availability does not remove those requirements.

details.title: Check the method, then check the fit
details.detail: OAuth2 managed availability is documented. This does not verify the scopes, token identity or organization policy needed by this assessment.
details.label: Verified requirement

details.title: Use your own consent identity
details.detail: You requested your app name on the provider consent screen. A custom auth config uses your provider credentials; branding the Connect Link alone does not change provider consent identity.
details.label: Recommendation

details.title: Scope classification follows the selected actions
details.detail: At least one selected scope is restricted. Reducing access to send-only changes this assessment.
details.label: Verified requirement

details.title: Separate granted permissions from agent tools
details.detail: The chosen scope can permit sending. Limit exposed tools and require product approval for sends where appropriate; tool restrictions do not narrow the provider-issued scope.
details.label: Recommendation
